title: What If a Whale Sank to the Ocean Floor? A Feast for Decades

scenes.text: What if a whale died and sank to the deep seafloor? It becomes a feast that lasts decades.
First, scavengers move in. For months to about a year and a half they strip off around 40 to 60 kilograms a day.
A 40-ton carcass delivers about as much carbon as the seafloor normally gets in roughly two thousand years.
Then bone-eating Osedax worms settle in, and on one North Pacific whale fall scientists counted 43 species.
When the flesh is gone, microbes feed on fats in the bones, and that stage can last for decades.
One death turns a barren patch of seabed into an oasis, with life living off a single whale for decades.

description:
What if a whale sank to the bottom of the deep ocean?
A single carcass can feed life on the seafloor for decades, from scavengers to bone-eating worms.
What should we run through next?
